title: Legal Services Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, SJA to CMC
raw_text:
2.     MOS 4421, Legal Services Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, SJA to CMC

    a. Summary. The Legal Services Specialist MOS encompasses every facet
of legal administration and management. General duties involve the
administrative support, research and investigation, client relations, and
technical and logistical support incident to a law center or staff judge
advocate office. Typical duties include research, preparation, and typing of
general correspondence, forms, reports, wills, powers of attorney, and other
documents dealing with legal and quasi-legal matters; checking all completed
work for typographic accuracy; maintaining office files; interacting with
clients; managing facilities and supplies; and if senior in grade, acting as
the legal services chief and senior enlisted advisor to the senior judge
advocate in the office, responsible for the overall assignment, performance,
training, counseling, morale, discipline, and welfare of all enlisted
personnel. Selected Marines may attend follow-on training at the Legal
Services Court Reporter Course to earn the NMOS 4422, Legal Services Court
Reporter.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must be U.S. citizen.

             (2) Must be a high school graduate or have obtained a GED.

             (3) Security requirement:   secret security clearance eligibility.

        (4) Must possess a CL score of 110 (not waiverable) or GT score of
105 or higher (waiverable to 102).

        (5) Marines requesting lateral move must meet the prerequisites for
PMOS 4421 and NMOS 4422.

        (6) Must have received no NJPs or been convicted by courts-martial or
civilian court for any offense involving controlled substances, sexual
misconduct, or moral turpitude.

       c.    Requirements

        (1) Demonstrate a typing proficiency of 25 words per minute and
complete that Legal Services Specialist Course (N0558X1).

        (2) Marines assigned to OccFld 44 through recruit accession or
lateral move are required to attend the formal Legal Services Specialist
Course (N0558X1) at Naval Justice School, Naval Station, Newport, RI. Upon

completion of this course, MOS 4421 is assigned.       MOJT to obtain the 4421
PMOS is not authorized.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (bh), Legal Services Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Law Clerks 23-2092.

            (2) Legal Secretaries 43-6012.

            (3) Paralegals and Legal Assistants 23-2011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Administrative Specialist, 0111.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
